mainTopic: Oil for the baked מנחות (mixing, smearing, pouring) and breaking מנחות into pieces
overview: This amud first finishes a comparison between the two pan מנחות, the מחבת and the מרחשת: both get oil in the vessel first, pouring, and mixing. Next comes the argument between רבי and the חכמים over whether the oil is mixed in after baking, as loaves, or before baking, as flour. A ברייתא gives each side's פסוק and lays out each side's full order of work. The גמרא then explains that mixing as loaves is 'impossible' because a רביעית of oil cannot be spread over many loaves. Next, the גמרא learns from the פסוקים that oven-baked חלות are only mixed and רקיקין are only smeared, in the shape of a Greek chi (X). Two ברייתות disagree about whether the wafers are covered completely or just marked with an X, and what happens to the leftover oil. A new משנה teaches that every מנחה made in a vessel is broken into pieces, but the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים are not. The amud ends by asking how the word 'היא' is known to exclude the wafers from pouring rather than the מנחת כהנים.

steps.title: Both pan offerings share the same oil steps
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is completed: the מרחשת needs oil in the vessel first, like the מחבת. The מחבת needs pouring and mixing, like the מרחשת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as here (the deep pan) oil is put into the vessel first, so too there (the shallow pan) oil is put into the vessel first. And just as there pouring and mixing are needed, so too here pouring and mixing are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a comparison it began just before this. Each of the two pan מנחות borrows the oil steps of the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק teaches oil-in-the-vessel-first about one pan offering. Other פסוקים teach pouring and mixing about the other pan offering. By linking the two, all three oil steps end up applying to both.

keyTerms.meaning: Putting oil into the empty vessel before the flour
Pouring oil on top
Mixing the oil in
The מנחה made in a shallow pan
The מנחה made in a deep pan

steps.whatToRemember: The מחבת and the מרחשת both get oil in the vessel first, pouring, and mixing.

phrases.english: Just as here – placing oil in a vessel [first],
phrases.notes: "Here" means the deep-pan מנחה (מרחשת), and "there" means the shallow-pan מנחה (מחבת).

phrases.english: so too there – placing oil in a vessel [first].
And just as there – pouring and mixing,
so too here – pouring and mixing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה כָּאן – מַתַּן שֶׁמֶן בִּכְלִי, אַף לְהַלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a derivation begun before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Oil in the vessel first, pouring, and mixing apply to both the מחבת and the מרחשת.

steps.title: The משנה: mix as loaves or as flour?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's argument. רבי says the oil is mixed into the baked loaves. The חכמים say it is mixed into the flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: Loaves: he mixes them with oil. These are the words of רבי. The חכמים say: it is mixed as fine flour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה to begin discussing it. It sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree there must be mixing. They argue only about when it happens. רבי says after baking, once the loaves are broken into pieces. The חכמים say before baking, while it is still flour.

keyTerms.meaning: Loaves, the baked form of the מנחה
He mixes them with oil
Fine flour, before baking

phrases.english: Loaves – he mixes them [with oil],
these are the words of Rabbi;
and the Sages say: [he mixes it as] fine flour.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַלּוֹת – בּוֹלְלָן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: mix after baking; חכמים: mix as flour before baking.

steps.title: Each side's פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the source for each side. The חכמים use "סלת בלולה" and רבי uses "חלות בלולות".
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "Fine flour mixed" teaches that it is mixed while it is flour. רבי says: he mixes the loaves, as it says "loaves mixed."
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the פסוק behind each opinion in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים read the word "mixed" as describing the flour, so the mixing happens before baking. רבי reads the same word as describing the loaves, so the mixing happens after baking.

keyTerms.meaning: "Fine flour mixed" (with oil), the פסוק for the חכמים
"Loaves mixed" (with oil), the פסוק for רבי

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "fine flour mixed" [with oil]
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:5

phrases.english: teaches that it is mixed while it is fine flour.
Rabbi says: as loaves he mixes them,
as it is said: "loaves mixed" [with oil].
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:4

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״סֹלֶת בְּלוּלָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sources for the two opinions in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים learn from "סלת בלולה"; רבי learns from "חלות בלולות".

steps.title: The חכמים challenge רבי from the תודה loaves
steps.stepSummary: The תודה loaves are also called "חלות", yet they can only be mixed as flour. So the word "חלות" does not prove that mixing happens after baking.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: About the loaves of the תודה, the תורה also says "loaves." Yet it is impossible to mix them once they are loaves; it must be done when they are flour!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי's proof by pointing to another place where the Torah uses the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's proof depends on the word "חלות". The חכמים show that the same word is used for the תודה loaves. Those loaves are clearly mixed as flour. So the word only names what the flour will become, not when the mixing happens.

keyTerms.meaning: The breads brought with a thanks offering
"But is it not so that...", a challenge
It is impossible

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying the פסוק is wrong to call them "loaves." They are saying the word "loaves" does not tell us when the mixing is done.

phrases.english: They said to him:
But regarding the breads of the thanks offering,
is it not said about them "loaves,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12

phrases.english: and it is impossible to mix them when they are loaves,
but only [when they are] fine flour!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי's proof from step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word is used for the תודה loaves, which are mixed as flour. So the word cannot prove that mixing happens after baking.

steps.title: The full process according to the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: Oil goes in the vessel, then the flour, then more oil and mixing. Then come kneading, baking, breaking into pieces, more oil, and taking the handful.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it? He puts oil in a vessel before making them, then puts in the flour. He puts oil on it and mixes it, kneads it, bakes it, and breaks it into pieces. He puts oil on it again, and takes a handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains, step by step, how the baked מנחות are made according to the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three oil steps show up in order. First comes oil in the vessel. Then comes mixing while it is still flour, as the חכמים hold. Pouring comes last, after the pieces are broken. Only then is the handful taken for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: How does he do it?
He kneads it
He breaks it into pieces
He takes a handful for the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים the order is: oil in the vessel, flour, oil and mixing, kneading, baking, breaking, oil again, and then the handful.

phrases.english: How does he do it?
He puts oil in a vessel before making them,
and puts it [the flour] in,
and puts oil on it and mixes it,
and kneads it, and bakes it, and breaks it into pieces,
and puts oil on it, and takes a handful.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד עוֹשֶׂה? נוֹתֵן שֶׁמֶן בִּכְלִי קוֹדֶם לַעֲשִׂיָּיתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the practical process following the חכמים' view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order of preparation: oil in the vessel, flour, oil and mixing, kneading, baking, breaking, oil (pouring), and the handful.

steps.title: רבי's method: mix the oil after baking
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that the oil is mixed into the חלות after they are baked. He learns this from the words "חלות בלולות בשמן" and lays out the full order of the work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: once they are loaves, he mixes them with oil, as the פסוק says, "loaves mixed with oil." How is it done? He puts oil in a vessel before anything else, puts in the flour, kneads it, and bakes it. Then he breaks it into pieces, puts oil on it, and mixes it. Then he puts oil on it again and takes the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי's side. He says the mixing with oil happens after the dough is baked into loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 gave the חכמים's order, where the oil is mixed into raw flour. רבי's order is almost the same, but the mixing moves to after baking: bake, break into pieces, then mix. He reads "חלות בלולות" to mean that the loaves themselves get mixed.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes back and puts (oil) on again

phrases.english: Rabbi says: as loaves, he mixes them,
phrases.notes: He means the oil is mixed in after the dough has already become baked loaves.

phrases.english: as it says: "loaves mixed with oil."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:4

phrases.english: How does he do it?
He puts oil in a vessel before making it,
and puts it in, and kneads it, and bakes it,
phrases.notes: "Puts it in" means he puts the flour into the vessel.

phrases.english: and breaks it into pieces, and puts oil on it, and mixes it,
and again puts oil on it, and takes the handful.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: חַלּוֹת בּוֹלְלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by giving רבי's order of work, set against the חכמים's order in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, the מנחה is baked first, then broken into pieces and mixed with oil, and then oil is poured on it again before the קמיצה.

steps.title: Why did the Rabbis say it is impossible?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חכמים meant when they told רבי in the ברייתא that mixing the loaves is "impossible."
steps.simpleTranslation: The "it is impossible" that the Rabbis said to רבי: what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the ברייתא. There the חכמים told רבי that loaves cannot be mixed, and the גמרא wants to know why. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only says "אי אפשר" about the תודה loaves and does not explain what makes mixing them as loaves impossible. The גמרא is looking for the practical problem behind the objection.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible
What is it? (what does it mean?)

phrases.english: The "it is impossible" that they said to him,
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים' objection from the ברייתא, about the תודה loaves in step 4.

phrases.english: the Rabbis to רבי: what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אִי אֶפְשָׁר״ דְּקָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי, מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי's method has been laid out, the גמרא asks why the חכמים rejected it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical problem makes רבי's method of mixing after baking impossible?

steps.title: Too little oil for many baked loaves
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק explains that there is only a רביעית of oil, and that small amount cannot be spread through many baked loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said: it is only a quarter-לוג of oil. How can it be divided among several loaves?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The problem is the amount of oil: there is too little to mix into baked loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw flour soaks up a small amount of oil easily, but baked loaves broken into pieces need much more to be truly mixed. Since only a רביעית is used, the mixing must happen while it is still flour, as the חכמים say.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a לוג, a small amount of liquid
Is divided up / spread out

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said:
it is only a quarter-לוג of oil,
how can it be divided among several loaves?

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים say mixing after baking is "impossible" because a רביעית of oil is too little to mix into many baked loaves.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: רְבִיעִית שֶׁמֶן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The small amount of oil (a רביעית) cannot be spread over many baked loaves, so the mixing must be done while it is still flour.

steps.title: משנה: loaves are mixed, wafers are smeared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: חלות need בלילה (mixing) and רקיקין need משיחה (smearing).
steps.simpleTranslation: The loaves need mixing, and the wafers need smearing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about the oven-baked מנחה. This sets up the ברייתא that gives the source for the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of oven-baked מנחה: thick חלות and thin רקיקין. The משנה gives each its own way of adding oil: the חלות are mixed with oil and the רקיקין are smeared with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing oil into the flour
Smearing oil on the surface
Thin wafers

phrases.english: The loaves require mixing,
and wafers require smearing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַחַלּוֹת טְעוּנוֹת בְּלִילָה, וּרְקִיקִין מְשִׁיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי and חכמים argument and quotes the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oven-baked חלות get בלילה; oven-baked רקיקין get משיחה.

steps.title: Only loaves are mixed, not wafers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "חלות בלולות" that רקיקין are not mixed. Without the פסוק, a קל וחומר would have said they should be.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "loaves mixed," but wafers are not mixed. For one could have said: isn't it logical? If loaves, which do not need smearing, need mixing, then wafers, which do need smearing, should surely need mixing too! So the פסוק says "loaves mixed," and not wafers mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the source in the פסוק for why רקיקין are not mixed. First it shows a קל וחומר that would have given the wrong answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר goes like this: חלות get fewer oil treatments (no smearing) and still get mixing, so רקיקין, which do get smearing, should get mixing too. The פסוק blocks this by saying only "חלות" are "בלולות".

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it logical? (opens a קל וחומר)
Reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter one
The פסוק teaches (to block the wrong conclusion)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "loaves mixed,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:4

phrases.english: but not wafers mixed.
For one could have said: isn't it logical?
If loaves, which do not require smearing,
require mixing,
then wafers, which do require smearing,
isn't it logical that they require mixing!
So the verse teaches: "loaves mixed,"
and not wafers mixed.

steps.confusionAlert: The קל וחומר here is not the conclusion. It is the mistaken reasoning that the פסוק comes to block.
steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״חַלּוֹת בְּלוּלֹת״, וְלֹא רְקִיקִין בְּלוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוק for the first half of the משנה's rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording "חלות בלולות" (ויקרא 2:4) limits mixing to חלות, overriding a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Only wafers are smeared, not loaves
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from "רקיקין משוחים" that חלות are not smeared. Again, a reverse קל וחומר is blocked by the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Wafers smeared," and not loaves smeared. For one could have said: isn't it logical? If wafers, which do not need mixing, need smearing, then loaves, which do need mixing, should surely need smearing too! So the פסוק says "wafers smeared," and not loaves smeared.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא does the mirror image of the last step. It proves from the פסוק that חלות are not smeared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the קל וחומר runs the other way: רקיקין get no mixing and still get smearing, so חלות, which do get mixing, should get smearing too. The פסוק says only "רקיקין" are "משוחים", so each kind of bread keeps just its own treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: Smeared (with oil)
For one might have thought
Is it not logical? (the end of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: "Wafers smeared,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:4

phrases.english: and not loaves smeared.
For one could have said: isn't it logical?
If wafers, which do not require mixing,
require smearing,
then loaves, which do require mixing,
isn't it logical that they require smearing!
So the verse teaches: "wafers smeared,"
and not loaves smeared.

steps.whatToRemember: חלות are only mixed and רקיקין are only smeared. The פסוק's exact wording blocks a קל וחומר in each direction.
steps.triggerLanguage: ״רְקִיקִין מְשׁוּחִין״, וְלֹא חַלּוֹת מְשׁוּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 10 for the second half of the משנה's rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording "רקיקין משוחים" (ויקרא 2:4) limits smearing to רקיקין, overriding a reverse קל וחומר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each type of oven-baked מנחה gets only its own oil treatment: חלות get בלילה, רקיקין get משיחה.

steps.title: What is the source for keeping mixing and smearing separate?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we really know from the פסוק that רקיקין are not mixed and חלות are not smeared.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the derivation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the real reasoning behind the ברייתא's derivation. It is setting up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the words 'חלות בלולות' and 'רקיקין משוחים' block the קל וחומר. But maybe the פסוק is just describing one example, and both actions could apply to both kinds of bread. The גמרא wants to know why the פסוק should be read as excluding.

keyTerms.meaning: The learning, the derivation from a פסוק

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּלְמוּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the derivations in steps 10 and 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק's descriptions are read as limits rather than mere examples.

steps.title: רבא: The תורה never writes 'smeared loaves' or 'mixed wafers'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that if both actions applied to both breads, the תורה should have written 'smeared חלות and mixed רקיקין' somewhere. Since it never did, each action belongs only to its own type.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The תורה should not have left it out completely. Let it write, 'smeared loaves and mixed wafers.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why the פסוק shows that the actions are exclusive. The תורה never describes the opposite combination anywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חלות could also be smeared and רקיקין could also be mixed, we would expect the תורה to mention that at least once. The complete silence shows that mixing is only for חלות and smearing is only for רקיקין. This is why the קל וחומר from steps 10 and 11 is blocked.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it skip or leave out
Smeared (with oil)
Mixed (with oil)

steps.whatToRemember: The תורה only ever says mixed חלות and smeared רקיקין, never the reverse. So each action belongs only to its own kind of bread.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Let it not skip it, and let it write
phrases.notes: He means: if both actions were allowed, the תורה should not have left this out completely. It should have written it somewhere.

phrases.english: 'Smeared loaves and mixed wafers.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לִישְׁתְּמִיט וְלִכְתּוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה never mentions the reverse combination anywhere, so the descriptions are exclusive.

steps.title: The משנה: smearing in the shape of a כי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the רקיקין are smeared in a shape like a 'כי', and the rest of the oil is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one smear them? Like a כי, and the rest is eaten, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. This sets up a question about what 'כמין כי' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches two things: the oil goes on the רקיקין in a particular shape, and the leftover oil is not used for the offering but is eaten. The unclear word 'כי' is explained in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: How?
In a shape like the letter 'כי'

phrases.english: How does one smear them? In a shape like a chi,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the רקיקין, the thin wafers.

phrases.english: and the rest is eaten, etc.
phrases.notes: 'The rest' is the leftover oil. 'Etc.' means the משנה continues.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד מוֹשְׁחָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after finishing the derivation about mixing and smearing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רקיקין are smeared in a כי shape and the leftover oil is eaten.

steps.title: What does 'like a כי' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what shape the משנה means by 'כמין כי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'like a כי'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'כי' in the משנה means. It sets up רב כהנא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כי' is not a normal Hebrew word or letter, so the shape is unclear. The גמרא wants to know exactly how the oil is drawn on the wafer.

phrases.english: What is 'like a chi'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי כְּמִין כִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the משנה just quoted.

steps.title: רב כהנא: The Greek letter X
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that 'כי' is the Greek letter chi, which looks like an X.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Like a Greek chi.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers that 'כי' is a Greek letter. The oil is smeared in an X shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Greek letter chi is written as X. So the כהן draws two crossing lines of oil on each wafer instead of covering it completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Greek

steps.whatToRemember: According to the משנה, the רקיקין are smeared with oil in an X shape.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Like a Greek chi.
phrases.notes: The Greek letter chi looks like an X.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא כְּמִין כִּי יְוָונִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כי' is the Greek letter chi, the shape X.

steps.title: A ברייתא: half חלות and half רקיקין, the wafers smeared all over
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a מנחה of half חלות and half רקיקין uses one לוג of oil, split in half. The רקיקין are smeared over their whole surface, and leftover oil goes back into the חלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A מנחה that comes half loaves and half wafers: he brings a לוג of oil and divides it, half for the loaves and half for the wafers. He mixes the loaves and smears the wafers. He smears the wafer over its whole surface, and he puts the rest of the oil back into the loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a mixed מנחה made of both kinds of bread. The first opinion explains how the oil is divided and used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לוג of oil is split evenly between the two kinds of bread. In this opinion the wafers are covered completely, not just in an X. Any oil left over from smearing is not wasted or eaten; it is mixed into the חלות.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of liquid; the amount of oil for this מנחה
He divides it in half
Over its whole surface
He returns it

steps.confusionAlert: This first opinion does not agree with the X shape from the משנה. It says to cover the whole wafer, and the leftover oil goes to the חלות, not to the כהנים.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחָה הַבָּאָה מֶחֱצָה חַלּוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה רְקִיקִין,
phrases.english: A meal offering that comes as half loaves and half wafers,
he brings a log of oil and divides it:
half of it for the loaves and half of it for the wafers.
The loaves he mixes, and the wafers he smears,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹשֵׁחַ אֶת הָרָקִיק עַל פְּנֵי כּוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: and he smears the wafer over its entire surface,
and the rest of the oil he returns to the loaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן מִנְחָה הַבָּאָה מֶחֱצָה חַלּוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה רְקִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that deals with the smearing and the leftover oil from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Split the לוג evenly; smear the wafers completely; put leftover oil into the חלות.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's view: X shape, leftover oil eaten by the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יהודה, quoting רבי שמעון, disagrees: the wafers are smeared in an X shape, and the leftover oil is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: He smears them like a כי, and the rest of the oil is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא disagrees with the first. It matches what our משנה said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two differences from the first opinion. The wafers get only an X of oil, not a full covering. The leftover oil does not go back into the חלות but is eaten by the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
Eaten by the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: First opinion: smear the whole wafer, leftover oil goes into the חלות. רבי שמעון: smear an X, leftover oil is eaten by the כהנים, just like the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
He smears them in a shape like a chi,
and the rest of the oil is eaten by the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smear the wafers in an X shape; the leftover oil is eaten by the כהנים.

steps.title: Wafers brought alone use up the whole log of oil
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא teaches that when רקיקין are brought by themselves, the כהן smears them again and again until the whole לוג of oil is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: when wafers are brought by themselves, the כהן takes a לוג of oil and smears them, then smears them again, and keeps going until all the oil in the לוג is used up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא, this time about a מנחה made only of wafers. The first opinion says the כהן keeps smearing until every drop of the לוג is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the wafers were only half the offering, so they got half a לוג. Here the wafers are the whole offering, so they get the full לוג. Nothing is left over, because all the oil goes onto the wafers.

keyTerms.meaning: Thin wafers baked for a מנחה
By themselves, not mixed with חלות
A measure of liquid; the amount of oil for one מנחה

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
Wafers that come by themselves,
he brings a לוג of oil and smears them,
and he smears them again,
until all the oil in the לוג is used up.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא about wafers brought alone, following the half-and-half ברייתא of steps 17-18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wafers brought alone are smeared again and again until the whole לוג is used up.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: smear in an X, and the leftover oil is eaten
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יהודה, quoting רבי שמעון, says the wafers are smeared in an X shape, and the rest of the oil is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: he smears them in the shape of a 'כי', and the rest of the oil is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion. He says the wafers only get an X shape of oil, and whatever oil is left goes to the כהנים to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same view רבי שמעון held in step 18 for the half-and-half case. He holds that smearing is just a mark in an X shape, not using up all the oil. So for him there is always leftover oil, and it is eaten by the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: In the shape of the Greek letter chi, like an X (see step 16)
The rest of the oil, what is left over after smearing
Is eaten by the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says to smear until the oil is gone. רבי שמעון says to smear an X, and the leftover oil is eaten by the כהנים. He holds this both for wafers brought alone and for half-and-half מנחות.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
He smears them in a shape like a chi,
and the rest of the oil is eaten by the כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wafers are smeared in an X shape, and the leftover oil is eaten by the כהנים.

steps.title: משנה: every מנחה made in a vessel must be broken into pieces
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that all מנחות prepared in a vessel require פתיתה, breaking into pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All the מנחות that are prepared in a vessel need to be broken into pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new משנה with a new topic. Every מנחה made in a vessel has to be broken into pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was how to put oil on the מנחה. Now the משנה adds a different step in making a מנחה: breaking it into pieces. Notice the limit 'made in a vessel'; the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Breaking the baked מנחה into pieces
That are prepared in a vessel
Require, need

phrases.english: משנה: All the מנחות
that are prepared in a vessel
require breaking into pieces.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַמְּנָחוֹת הַנַּעֲשׂוֹת בִּכְלִי טְעוּנוֹת פְּתִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new subject (breaking into pieces).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All מנחות prepared in a vessel require פתיתה.

steps.title: What do the words 'in a vessel' leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which מנחות the משנה means to exclude by saying 'prepared in a vessel'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is this meant to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה added the words 'prepared in a vessel.' It wants to know which offerings these words are meant to exclude, and it is setting up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have just said 'all מנחות need breaking.' Since it added a limit, there must be some offering that falls outside it. The גמרא wants to know which one.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה
To exclude what? The question of which case a phrase leaves out

phrases.english: גמרא: To exclude what?
phrases.notes: He means: which offerings do the words 'prepared in a vessel' leave out?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the limiting phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which offerings are left out by the words 'הנעשות בכלי'.

steps.title: רב פפא: it leaves out the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the words 'in a vessel' exclude the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים from the requirement of breaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It leaves out the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. The שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים do not need to be broken into pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two bread offerings are baked in an oven and are not prepared in a vessel like the pan מנחות. So the משנה's rule of breaking does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves offered on שבועות from the new wheat
The twelve loaves placed on the שולחן in the היכל each שבת

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
To exclude the two loaves
and the לחם הפנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא לְמַעוֹטֵי שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase excludes the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים from פתיתה.

steps.title: The פסוק includes all מנחות in breaking
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word 'מנחה' in the פסוק 'פתות אתה פתים... מנחה' that all מנחות need breaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'You shall break it in pieces... it is a מנחה.' This comes to include all the מנחות in the requirement of breaking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows the source in the פסוק for breaking מנחות. The extra word 'מנחה' teaches that the rule covers all מנחות, not just the pan offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is speaking about the מנחת מחבת, the pan offering. But it ends with the word 'מנחה', which the ברייתא reads as stretching the rule to every kind of מנחה. This step is also setting up the question that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall break it in pieces (ויקרא ב:ו)
To include, to widen the rule to more cases

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'You shall break it in pieces... a מנחה' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:6

phrases.english: to include all the מנחות in breaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן פָּתוֹת אֹתָהּ פִּתִּים מִנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the משנה's rule that all מנחות need breaking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'מנחה' in the פסוק includes all מנחות in the requirement of פתיתה.

steps.title: Maybe the שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים are included too?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that since all מנחות are included, maybe the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים must also be broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might think that I should include even the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: if 'מנחה' includes everything, maybe even these two bread offerings need breaking. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the rule was widened to 'all מנחות', it might seem to cover every flour offering. The ברייתא states this possible reading only so that it can push it back.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think, a reading the ברייתא is about to reject
Include

steps.confusionAlert: This 'יכול' is not the final הלכה. It is a possible reading that the ברייתא raises only to reject it in the next line.

phrases.english: One might think that I include
even the two loaves and the לחם הפנים?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the inclusion of step 24 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the wide inclusion also covers the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: The word 'אותה' leaves them out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the word 'אותה' (it) limits the rule, so the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים are not broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'אותה', 'it'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The word 'אותה' narrows the rule, so the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים do not need breaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has a word that includes ('מנחה') and a word that limits ('אותה'). Together they mean all regular מנחות are broken, but these two bread offerings are not. This gives a פסוק as the source for רב פפא's answer in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; introduces the word in the פסוק that settles the question
'It'; a word that limits the rule

steps.whatToRemember: All מנחות prepared in a vessel need פתיתה (learned from 'מנחה'). The שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים are left out (learned from 'אותה'), just as רב פפא said.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'it.'
phrases.notes: 'It' points to the specific מנחה in the פסוק, which limits the rule so it does not reach these two bread offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר אֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possible reading of step 25 using the word 'אותה'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'אותה' excludes the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים from פתיתה.

steps.title: All meal offerings need oil poured on them
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word 'מנחה' in the פסוק that all מנחות need pouring of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'And you shall pour oil upon it, it is a meal offering.' This comes to include all the meal offerings in the rule of pouring oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now turns from breaking the מנחה to pouring oil on it. It uses the same פסוק to say that every מנחה needs oil poured on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like step 24. There the word 'מנחה' included all מנחות in breaking, and here the same word includes all מנחות in pouring. The ברייתא starts with a broad rule and will narrow it in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Pouring oil onto the מנחה
To include (a word in the פסוק adds more cases)

phrases.english: "And you shall pour ... oil, a meal offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:6. The dots skip the word עליה (upon it), which the ברייתא uses in step 29.

phrases.english: to include all the meal offerings in pouring.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיָצַקְתָּ שָׁמֶן מִנְחָה לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל הַמְּנָחוֹת לִיצִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same method as step 24, now for pouring instead of breaking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'מנחה' includes all מנחות in the rule of pouring oil.

steps.title: Maybe even the oven-baked offering needs pouring
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the broad rule also covers the oven-baked מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think I should include even the oven-baked meal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: if 'all מנחות' need pouring, maybe that includes the oven-baked מנחה too. This sets up the next step, where the פסוק will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The broad word 'מנחה' seems to include everything. The ברייתא tests whether the מנחת מאפה is also covered, so it can show how the פסוק limits the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might think' (opens a mistaken idea that the ברייתא will reject)
The meal offering baked in an oven

phrases.english: One might think that I include
even the oven-baked meal offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף מִנְחַת מַאֲפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the broad rule of step 27 goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule of pouring also apply to the oven-baked מנחה?

steps.title: 'Upon it' leaves out the oven-baked offering
steps.stepSummary: The words 'עליה שמן' limit the pouring, so the oven-baked מנחה is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'oil upon it,' meaning upon this מנחה and not upon the oven-baked one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the words 'עליה שמן' (oil upon it). The word 'it' points to one kind of מנחה, so the oven-baked מנחה does not get oil poured on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מנחה' includes, and 'עליה' limits. The limit takes the מנחת מאפה out of the rule of pouring.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Upon it': a word that limits the rule to one kind of מנחה
'The פסוק teaches': introduces the answer from the פסוק

phrases.english: The verse states: "oil upon it."
phrases.notes: 'Upon it' means upon this מנחה only, not the oven-baked one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר עָלֶיהָ שָׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'עליה' leaves the oven-baked מנחה out of pouring.

steps.title: Maybe only the loaves are left out, not the wafers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether only the loaves of the oven-baked מנחה are left out, while the wafers still need pouring.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should I leave out only the loaves and not leave out the wafers?
steps.whatsHappening: The oven-baked מנחה can come as loaves (חלות) or as wafers (רקיקין). The ברייתא asks whether only the loaves are left out of pouring, and this sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 left out the oven-baked מנחה. The ברייתא now checks whether that covers both forms it can come in, or only the loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Loaves (thick baked cakes)
Wafers (thin baked pieces)
I will leave out (exclude from the rule)

phrases.english: Should I exclude the loaves
but not exclude the wafers?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹצִיא אֶת הַחַלּוֹת וְלֹא אוֹצִיא אֶת הָרְקִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the exclusion of step 29 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the wafers of the oven-baked מנחה also left out of pouring, or only the loaves?

steps.title: 'It' leaves out the wafers too
steps.stepSummary: The word 'היא' teaches that the wafers are also left out of pouring.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'it is a meal offering,' which teaches that the wafers are also left out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with the word 'היא' (it). That word limits the rule again, so the wafers also do not get oil poured on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each limiting word does its own job. 'עליה' left out the loaves, and 'היא' adds that the wafers are left out as well. So the whole oven-baked מנחה is free from pouring.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It': another limiting word in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Pouring: 'מנחה' includes all מנחות. 'עליה שמן' leaves out the oven-baked loaves, and 'היא' leaves out the oven-baked wafers.

phrases.english: The verse states: "It."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק: 'מנחה היא', it is a meal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30 and finishes the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'היא' leaves out the wafers as well.

steps.title: Why not say 'it' leaves out the priests' offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: how do we know 'היא' leaves out the wafers? Maybe it leaves out the מנחת כהנים instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the source for this? Let me say instead that 'it' comes to leave out the meal offering of priests!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the ברייתא's last step. It asks why the word 'היא' must mean the wafers, when it could just as easily leave out a different מנחה, the מנחת כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A limiting word tells us that something is left out, but not always what. The גמרא suggests a different target for 'היא', so the ברייתא's reading now needs support.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the source?': asks how the derivation works
'I could say': offers a different reading
The meal offering brought by a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the wafers do need pouring. It is only asking how we know that the word 'היא' is the source that leaves them out.

phrases.english: What is the derivation?
I could say it is to exclude the meal offering of priests!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּלְמוּדָא אֵימָא לְהוֹצִיא מִנְחַת כֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of 'היא' given in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that 'היא' leaves out the wafers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A limiting word could point to a different exclusion, the מנחת כהנים, so it is not clear that it refers to the wafers.
